title: Seller wiring diagram playbook (frag)
body:
Purpose
---
This is a working fragment: a lightweight playbook + wiring diagram to help sellers and SEs trace the path from account qualifying signals to the recommended operational fallback and escalation sequence.

Why this exists
- Sellers are often stuck translating product-level tradeoffs (latency vs. cost vs. quality) into clear negotiation and pilot plans for platform teams.
- Existing cheat sheets list options; this doc ties signals -> choices -> scripts so reps can act quickly in a call.
- Focus is on the first 3 pilot calls and the operative handoff to Customer Engineering/Platform.

Audience
- AE/SE running pilot qualification calls with engineering or platform teams
- SDRs prepping for technical discovery for mid-market/enterprise accounts
- Field ops that will own the canary + fallback runbook during the pilot

High-level wiring (one-liner)
- Observe signal on call -> pick default routing & model variant -> propose pilot configuration (burst vs reserved capacity, quantization, caching) -> document SLOs & rollback triggers -> commit pilot sequencing and who runs it.

Quick decision map (textual diagram)
- If latency-sensitive (<300ms p95) -> recommend: low-latency model variant + reserved capacity OR Redwood Dedicated trial -> Canary scope: small prod-like data subset; add tracing hooks.
- Else if cost-sensitive & high throughput -> recommend: quantized variant + batching + prefix cache -> Pilot: synthetic load test + token-cost dashboard.
- Else if sensitive data/regulatory -> recommend: Private deployment (VPC) + audit retention -> Pilot: isolated staging VPC, KMS integration proof.

Signal checklist (what we ask on call)
- Traffic pattern: peak qps, average qps, typical sequence length (tokens)
- Latency SLO (p50/p95) and p95 percentile the customer cares about
- Cost constraint or target (dollars per 1M tokens or per interaction)
- Data sensitivity (PII, PHI) and retention/archival needs
- Integration constraints: on-prem firewall, egress rules, cert pinning
- Success metrics for pilot (accuracy thresholds, user engagement lift, error budget)

Recommended pilot bundles (one-paragraph quick-sell)
- Latency-first bundle: Redwood Dedicated trial (2–4 GPUs), low-latency model variant, direct routing to dedicated pool, 1-week canary with real traffic (sampled 5%), SLA: p95 < requested threshold, rollback policy: route to hosted model variant.
- Cost-first bundle: Hosted API with quantized model + intelligent batching + prefix caching, 2-week pilot with synthetic stress window, weekly cost telemetry share, fallback: raise batch size or switch to larger reserved capacity if latency degrades.
- Regulated-data bundle: Private deployment sandbox, KMS integration verification, audit logs enabled, 3-week isolated on-prem proof-of-concept, sign-off: security review + SCC audit checklist.

Seller scripts (micro-scripts to use live)
- Qualify: "Can you share typical query size and how many requests per minute you expect during peak? If you don't have exact numbers, can we run a quick sample import?"
- Close to pilot: "Given your p95 target, our default would be X. We can provision a Dedicated pool for a short canary; if that sounds right I can schedule a handoff to platform engineering and propose a 2-week window with rollback triggers defined in advance."
- Objection (cost): "We can start on Hosted with quantization and caching to prove end-user impact, and then explore Reserved if the economics require it. That keeps your initial bill predictable while we measure model quality and latency."

Handoff checklist (minimum fields in the pilot ticket)
- Account name, primary contact, AE and SE owners
- Pilot bundle chosen (latency/cost/private) and short justification
- Traffic sample or CSV for representative requests
- Expected pilot dates (canary start/end), rollback triggers (error % or p95 breach)
- Required integrations (KMS, VPC peering, certs) and owners
- Evaluation criteria (quantitative metrics and pass/fail thresholds)

Troubleshooting playlets (short decision scripts)
- Symptom: p95 spikes during burst -> check: queueing at app layer, mis-sized pool, batch size settings. Quick action: temporarily reduce batch window and route critical traffic to a low-latency variant.
- Symptom: quality regression post-quantization -> check: model variant used, quantization profile, sampling of failing prompts. Quick action: rollback to higher-fidelity variant and log failing prompt set for model ops.
- Symptom: customer sees token cost creep -> check: soft-prompt lengths, response verbosity, caching hit-rate. Quick action: enable prefix caching or add guardrails to output length.

Operational escalation ladder
- Triage (SE/AE): first 4 hours, collect traces, sample prompts, validate config vs pilot doc
- Platform Ops: 4–24 hours, adjust routing, scale or throttle reserved pool, flip routing if needed
- Eng serving-runtime: 24+ hours or repeatable regression, run kernel/quantization inspection, deeper perf profiling

Speaker notes / SLIDES sketch (for a 6-slide deck to hand to AMs)
1. Title + One-liner: "Pilot wiring: How we map signals to config choices" (30s)
2. Call checklist & signals (1 slide, 1 min)
3. Decision map (diagram) mapping latency/cost/regulatory to pilot bundles (1 slide, 1 min)
4. Handoff ticket template (1 slide, show required fields) (45s)
5. Troubleshooting quick cards (2–3 scenarios) (1 slide, 1 min)
6. Next steps & ask (schedule handoff, sample data upload) (30s)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Build a small Airtable template for the handoff ticket fields so SEs don't forget keys
- Validate exact cost delta numbers for quantization vs standard models (need infra/finance data)
- Create a 1-pager for security teams that maps Redwood Private features to common audit controls (SOC2 items called out)
- Ask platform team if we can pre-provision a 2-GPU Dedicated sandbox for pilot acceleration (reduce lead time)

References / quick links (placeholders)
- Pilot ticket template (WIP Confluence) -> CONFLUENCE-GB-8342
- Example rollback policy (Jira) -> JIRA-OPS-4123
- SE scripts repo -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sales-assets/pull/58

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally terse — want something SEs can print/use in a 1:1. Keep language action-oriented.
- Prefer we keep the bundles opinionated (don't show 10 micro-variants) — sellers need a default.
- If you have concrete numbers for cost deltas or reserve lead times, drop them in the TODO section.

End fragment.
